item.description:
Changed

  • **Models that reason before answering pass admission.** The default generation output budget for llama.cpp admission rises from 256 to 4,096 tokens on every path: command line, MCP tools, the app's Upgrade Engine and placement controls, and fleet commands. At 256, reasoning models such as Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and Gemma 4 12B used the whole budget thinking and were refused as truncated while answering correctly. The contract is unchanged: the exact marker, a normal stop, the throughput floors and the latency limit still apply, and a model that already stopped within 256 tokens uses the same tokens as before. Admission receipts now record the budget they ran with, and fleet benchmark and deployment calls get the same one-hour deadline as maintenance, so a reasoning model's admission on another Mac is not cut off after 30 seconds.

Corrected

  • **Managed model downloads no longer leave a copy in the temporary folder.** The Hugging Face client Spire uses (swift-huggingface 0.9.0) copied each finished download into its cache and never removed the download's temporary file, so every managed deployment left a CFNetworkDownload_*.tmp clone of the model. On APFS the clone shares storage with the cached model, but it keeps that storage allocated after the model is removed. Spire now requires swift-huggingface 0.10.2, which removes it (upstream fix huggingface/swift-huggingface#65).

Security

  • **Agent access is read-only until a policy grants more.** With no agent policy file, spire and spire-mcp now deny every change. Before, spire apply and package-apply fell back to full operator permissions. Spire reads the policy named by SPIRE_BROKER_CONFIG, otherwise ~/.config/spire/broker.json in the account's home directory; $HOME and XDG_CONFIG_HOME are not consulted, so under sudo the home is root's. Name the policy explicitly for commands that change state.
  • **A named policy that does not exist is refused.** When SPIRE_BROKER_CONFIG names a missing file, Spire stops and says so instead of silently using the account's own policy, which can grant more.

Changed

  • **The container boot job runs under its own narrow policy.** catalog/boot/boot-broker.json grants only container listing, system status and deployment apply, and containers-boot.sh passes it to spire reconcile --repair. A Mac that runs the boot job needs both files in /Library/Application Support/Spire/ before it updates; without the policy the boot job's repairs are refused.

Corrected

  • **Unattended updates work on a Mac that serves no MLX host.** A Mac serving only llama.cpp roles could never finish a headless update or receive the update broker; every attempt rolled back. The updater now decides once, before changing anything, whether the Mac serves an MLX host, and records that decision in its journal. It proves an installation from what the update produced — bundle ownership, signature, build and source revision, the update broker's digest, the update check, and every llama role that answered before the update — without running bundle code as root. spire-mlx install-daemon on a Mac with no MLX models installs only the update check and broker, and refuses root as the serving account. A Mac whose installed updater predates this release needs the one-time procedure in docs/operations/HEADLESS_UPDATE_FIRST_HOP.md.
  • **Update recovery cannot jam or repeat itself.** A recorded success or rollback is proven again only against what that step installed, so a llama role removed afterwards no longer blocks every later update, and a rollback is never repeated on each run. When a recorded outcome genuinely cannot be proven again, the error names the documented way out, "Retiring a stuck update journal", which moves the journal aside rather than deleting it.
  • **launchd answers are read as macOS 26 actually gives them.** On a Mac with no desktop login, launchd answers a user-session query with exit 125 rather than "not found". Spire now treats only launchd's measured not-found answers as absent, on either output stream, and stops before changing anything on any other answer. This covers the update mode decision, the installation proof, MLX host status, uninstall and the competing-job check, and llama role suspend and resume.
  • **An engine upgrade can be retried after a failed admission.** A candidate that failed admission shares its model files with the live role, and removing it was always refused, so one rejected admission locked the role out of every later engine upgrade. Removing a placement now succeeds when another role uses the same files; deleting shared files is still refused.
  • **Model removal recovery keeps a role whose server may still be running.** A removal that stopped before Spire recorded the endpoint's state, and could not have deleted anything, now keeps the placement instead of removing the record of a server that may still be serving.

Corrected

  • **Managed model downloads work on Macs without a logged-in desktop session.** macOS reports zero "important usage" capacity when its space-accounting service is not running for the user, which made Spire refuse every managed download on headless machines despite ample free disk. Spire now falls back to the volume's plain available capacity, which excludes purgeable space and is therefore the more conservative figure. The 5 GiB reserve and the refusal on genuinely insufficient disk are unchanged.
